documents.instruction: Maintain the concise English documentation index and links to every Glina concept, interface, walkthrough, runbook, desktop, and examples page.
Explain what Glina is, its runtime-art and authoring-pipeline halves, hard external ownership boundaries, verification definition of done, and next-page links; remain public-safe.

Maintain an English quick start that distinguishes captured non-mutating evidence from stateful generation commands, includes observed CLI/verify/setup/config output, and never implies registry publication.
Describe Glina components, dependency and trust boundaries, data flow, ownership versus Skarbiec/Weles/Brama/Blender/Desktop, and process/artifact lifecycles.
Document every configuration key actually read by Glina with types, defaults, precedence/selection behavior, strict Skarbiec-only secret policy, environment behavior, and resolved handoff semantics.
Maintain the complete Glina CLI command, argument, output, side-effect, refusal, and exit-code reference, including the operational export-config command.
Document the full glina-mcp newline JSON-RPC protocol, handshake/errors, all six tools, exact schemas, return/refusal semantics, and captured verify evidence.
Document every loopback HTTP endpoint, request/response schema, NDJSON ordering and terminal status, queue behavior, limits, exact errors, and executed evidence.
Maintain a complete public JavaScript export reference including signatures, defaults, return/mutation contracts, environmental dependencies, subpaths, and loader stub behavior.
Explain the separate macOS companion's executable discovery, backend lifecycle, HTTP mappings, NDJSON consumption, refusals, and operator safety boundary without claiming desktop ownership for Glina.
Maintain a symptom-first operations runbook grounded in exact source refusal strings, safe probe order, recovery actions, and warnings before stateful live-Blender operations.
Index all runnable examples, external-system requirements, commands, already-captured outputs, and the no-live-Blender safety boundary.
Preserve the executed passing and deliberately failing structural verification walkthrough with exact observed statistics, thresholds, refusals, and exit interpretation.
Preserve the executed ephemeral loopback HTTP walkthrough with exact health and NDJSON verify evidence, consumer rules, and an explicit no-Blender-interaction boundary.
Explain the sculpt-job noun, model step contract, round loop, bridge-down invariant, export/gate lifecycle, result shape, and historical proven runs.
Explain the studio-job noun, every named step, config-driven selectors, download/postprocess/gate path, return shape, credentials boundary, and cleanup invariant.
Explain the verification-gate noun, structural and optional render layers, report/stats meaning, every threshold/default, lifecycle, and exact parser/gate refusals.
Explain the Blender-session noun, spawn/tool/environment boundaries, exception wrapping, import/export cleanup, real health probe, bridge port, and close invariants.
Explain the Weles browser-session noun, complete tool surface, lifecycle, timeout and exact refusals, scrubbed environment, and which allowlisted environment names are not actually consumed.
Explain Brama/OpenRouter backend selection exactly as implemented, transport signing/retry/deadline behavior, direct-provider refusal, message conversion, and reply parsing.
Explain the runtime-art noun, module responsibilities and host dependencies, card-art decisions, executed example evidence, and procedural-only loader stubs.
Maintain a portable, self-cleaning shell example that runs default verification and catches a deliberate multi-reason refusal without Blender, Weles, vault, or network use.
Maintain a portable, self-cleaning shell example that accepts a non-secret config and demonstrates exact inline-secret refusal without contacting the vault.
Maintain a portable, self-cleaning example that owns an ephemeral Glina backend, observes readiness and health, streams local verification, and reliably terminates it without Blender access.
Maintain a portable raw stdio MCP example covering initialize, initialized notification, tools/list, and local glina_verify_asset with an absent optional config.
Maintain a dependency-free Node example that imports the checkout's cardArtSvg, writes one dwarven rare forge SVG to a caller-selected or temporary path, and reports output size.
